// quicktest is imported as qt here, so the rules do apply -- but only where that
// name still means the import. This is the other half of binding R1 to the
// import: a nearer declaration takes the name over, and a rule that reduced the
// question to "is the receiver spelled qt" reports the two shadowed calls, while
// a rule that reduced it to "does this block declare qt anywhere" loses the one
// real violation, which is written before the declaration that shadows it.
package fixture

import (
	"testing"

	qt "github.com/frankban/quicktest"
)

type asserter struct{}

func (asserter) Assert(got, want int) {}

func (asserter) Check(got, want int) {}

func TestTargetShape(t *testing.T) {
	c := qt.New(t)
	c.Assert(1, qt.Equals, 1)
}

func TestShadowedThroughout(t *testing.T) {
	var qt asserter
	qt.Assert(2, 2)
	qt.Check(3, 3)

	t.Log("the package-level functions are not reachable in this scope")
}

func TestShadowedOnlyAfterTheDeclaration(t *testing.T) {
	qt.Assert(t, 4, qt.Equals, 4)

	qt := asserter{}
	qt.Assert(5, 5)

	t.Log("the first call is quicktest's and the second is not")
}
